content: Hi! How can I help you today with your SQL queries?
Hi, I need to write a query that lists every customer and their total number of orders. Could you help?
Sure! Which SQL database are you using? (e.g., Postgres, MySQL, BigQuery, Snowflake)

Great. Assuming you have tables named 'customers' and 'orders', with 'orders.customer_id' referencing 'customers.id', you can use this query:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
```
Thanks! What if I only want customers who have at least one order?

You can add a HAVING clause to filter for customers with orders:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0;
```
Is there a way to sort the results by the number of orders, most to least?

Absolutely. Just add ORDER BY:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0
ORDER BY total_orders DESC;
```
Suppose I want to include customers with zero orders at the bottom. What should I do?

Switch back to LEFT JOIN and remove the HAVING clause. Then, order with NULLs last:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_orders DESC NULLS LAST;
```
Can I show the date of the most recent order for each customer too?

Yes, you can use MAX() for that. Here's the query:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_orders DESC NULLS LAST;
```
Nice. Does Postgres have any functions to format the date in a specific way?

Yes. You can use TO_CHAR to format dates. For example, to show the date as 'YYYY-MM-DD':
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders, TO_CHAR(MAX(o.order_date), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS latest_order
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_orders DESC NULLS LAST;
```
If I want to limit the results to the top 10 customers by orders, how would that look?

Just add LIMIT 10 at the end:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders, TO_CHAR(MAX(o.order_date), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS latest_order
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_orders DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
```
Perfect. Last thing, what if I only want customers from California?

Add a WHERE clause for the state, assuming there's a column like c.state:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders, TO_CHAR(MAX(o.order_date), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS latest_order
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.state = 'CA'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_orders DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
```
